objective: The shop wants to know what the goods it sold cost, valued first in, first out (FIFO). Add a module `stockroom/costing.py`. Records: frozen dataclasses `CostMovement(day: datetime.date, sku: str, kind: str, quantity: int, unit_cost_cents: int | None = None)` (`kind` is `in` or `out`; `unit_cost_cents` is `None` for `out`) and `CostRow(month, sku, opening_qty, opening_value, in_qty, in_value, out_qty, out_value, closing_qty, closing_value)` with the fields in exactly this order (`month` is `YYYY-MM`, values are integer cents). `read_cost_movements(text) -> list[CostMovement]` reads a CSV text (the `csv` module) with the header `day,sku,kind,quantity,unit_cost`. Every cell is trimmed of spaces and tabs only (not other whitespace) before it is checked; rows whose cells are all empty after trimming are skipped; the header cells must equal those five names. Each other row has exactly five cells: `day` is exactly `YYYY-MM-DD` with ASCII digits and an existing date (no other ISO form such as `20240103`); `sku` is 2 to 4 ASCII capitals, `-`, 3 to 5 ASCII digits; `kind` is `in` or `out` exactly (lower case); `quantity` is ASCII digits only, at least 1 (`007` is 7); `unit_cost` for `in` is ASCII digits optionally followed by `.` and exactly two digits (`12` is 1200 cents, `0.05` is 5; no sign, symbol, grouping, single decimal or missing integer part), and for `out` it must be empty. Anything else, including a missing or wrong header and an empty text, is a `stockroom.errors.ParseError`. Movements come back in file order. `fifo_report(movements) -> list[CostRow]` takes any iterable. Movements are applied in order of `day`; movements of the same day keep their given order. Each SKU keeps a queue of cost layers: an `in` appends a layer of `quantity` units at its unit cost; an `out` takes its units from the oldest layers first (using up a layer before the next one), and its value is the sum of units times their layer's unit cost. An `out` of more units than the SKU has at that moment raises `stockroom.errors.StockError` whose message contains `YYYY-MM-DD SKU: short by N` (the movement's day, its SKU, and the missing units), even when a later movement would bring stock. The report has one row per month and SKU: the months run from the month of the earliest day to the month of the latest day, every calendar month included (also months without movements, across years); in each month every SKU whose first movement is in that month or earlier has a row (also when its stock is zero), rows ordered by month, then SKU in plain string order. `in_qty`/`in_value` and `out_qty`/`out_value` sum the month's movements of that SKU; the opening quantity and value are the previous month's closing ones (zero in the SKU's first month), and closing = opening + in - out for both quantity and value. No movements give `[]`. `average_cost(quantity, value) -> int | None` is `value / quantity` rounded to a whole cent with ties going to the even cent (round half to even, computed exactly on integers), and `None` when the quantity is 0. Finally add `python -m stockroom cogs --movements FILE [--month YYYY-MM]`. It prints one line per report row, `MONTH SKU open=Q/V in=Q/V out=Q/V close=Q/V avg=A` (opening, in, out, closing quantity and value), where each value V is `format_money(cents, symbol='')` (for example `12,340.01`) and A is `format_money(average_cost(closing_qty, closing_value), symbol='')` or `-` when the closing quantity is 0; then a last line `total cogs=V` with the sum of `out_value` over the printed rows. `--month` (exactly four digits, `-`, and a month `01` to `12`) prints only that month's rows (the costing still runs over the whole file), and only the total line when the month has no rows. Any error (bad file, shortage, bad `--month`) exits with code 1, `stockroom: error: ` followed by the error message on stderr, and empty stdout. Existing behaviour otherwise stays.
acceptance: `read_cost_movements` reads rows with trimmed cells, blank and all-empty rows skipped, `\r\n` line ends, `007`, `12` (1200), `0.05` and `1000.00`, gives `[]` for a header alone (also with spaces around header cells), and raises `ParseError` for 33 bad rows (`20240103`, `2024-1-3`, `2024-02-30`, `2024-W01-3`, lower-case or Arabic-Indic SKUs, `IN`, `move`, quantities `0`, `-1`, `+1`, `1.5`, an Arabic-Indic digit, `²`, `1_0`, a leading U+00A0 and a quoted `7` followed by a newline, unit costs `12.5`, `12.505`, `$12.50`, `"1,250.00"`, `-1.00`, `.50`, Arabic-Indic decimals, an inner U+00A0, `1_000.00`, a leading U+00A0, a quoted `1.00` followed by a newline, a quoted day followed by a newline, an empty cost for `in`, a cost for `out`, four or six cells) and for an empty text, a blank text and wrong headers

`fifo_report` takes units from the oldest layer first across several layers (17 units out of layers at 1.00, 1.30 and 0.90 cost 18.30 and leave 2 units worth 1.80), uses up a layer exactly before the next one, accepts an iterator in any day order, and gives `[]` for no movements

Every month from the first to the last is reported for every SKU already seen, across a year boundary, with opening equal to the previous closing, months without movements carried over, SKUs that start later appearing from their first month, a SKU at zero still listed, and rows ordered by month then SKU (`AB-100` before `MUG-001`)

Same-day movements keep their order (an `in` then an `out` of the same day works, the reverse raises `StockError` containing `2024-01-05 MUG-001: short by 2`), a shortage is not excused by a later `in` (`2024-01-06 MUG-001: short by 3`), an `out` of an unknown SKU fails (`2024-02-01 TEA-010: short by 1`), and an `out` listed before an `in` with an earlier day is applied after it

`average_cost(quantity, value)` rounds half to even: `average_cost(0, 0)` is `None`; `average_cost(2, 25)` is 12, and for the arguments `(2, 75)`, `(2, 125)`, `(2, 135)`, `(4, 10)`, `(4, 14)`, `(3, 100)`, `(3, 200)`, `(8, 4)`, `(8, 12)`, `(1, 999)` and `(6, 999)` it gives 38, 62, 68, 2, 4, 33, 67, 0, 2, 999 and 166; results are exact for quantities of 10^12

For 600 seeded random ledgers (up to 25 movements of three SKUs over up to 14 months, `out` never more than the stock at that point, unit costs up to 999.99): every row equals an independent FIFO computation of the stated rules, closing quantity and value equal opening + in - out and are never negative, each SKU's opening equals its previous month's closing, shuffling whole days (keeping the order inside a day) gives the same report, and the ledger written as CSV is read back by `read_cost_movements` unchanged

`python -m stockroom cogs --movements F` prints `2024-01 MUG-001 open=0/0.00 in=20/27.50 out=12/15.50 close=8/12.00 avg=1.50`, the carried-over February row, `avg=-` for a closing quantity of 0, `avg=0.75` for 3 units worth 2.26, and `total cogs=27.50`; `--month 2024-03` prints that month's two rows and `total cogs=12.00`, a month without rows prints only `total cogs=0.00`; grouped values such as `12,340.01` and `avg=12.33` for 1001 units; a header-only file prints `total cogs=0.00`; a shortage and `--month` values `2024-13` and `2024-3` exit with code 1, empty stdout and `stockroom: error:` (the shortage message names `2024-03-06 TEA-010: short by 1`)
